title: Is There a Route to the Hospital
real_world_story: The response system needs to know whether an ambulance can travel from its location to a hospital through any sequence of roads. The road network is modeled as a directed graph. Use a depth-first traversal to determine whether the hospital is reachable from the ambulance location.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Following roads as far as possible to discover whether a route exists

problem_statement: Given a directed graph with N nodes and M edges, and two nodes S and T, determine whether there is a path from S to T. Print YES if T is reachable from S, otherwise print NO.
task: Use DFS to check whether the hospital is reachable from the ambulance location.
input_format: The first line contains four integers N, M, S and T, where N is the number of nodes (numbered 1 to N), M is the number of directed edges, S is the ambulance location, and T is the hospital. The next M lines each contain two integers U and V indicating a directed road from node U to node V.
output_format: Print YES if node T is reachable from node S, otherwise print NO.

examples.explanation: A route to the hospital exists: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4, and also 1 -> 2 -> 4.
There is no road leading from node 1 toward node 4, so the hospital is unreachable.

expected_algorithm.name: Graph DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: DFS explores one connected route as far as possible and can determine whether the target is reachable using recursion or an explicit stack.

hint: Begin the traversal at the ambulance node S.
Visit a neighbor and follow it as far as possible before backtracking.
If the hospital T is visited, it is reachable.
real_world_takeaway: DFS helps an emergency-response system quickly confirm whether a hospital is reachable, identifying viable destinations early.
